finding.title: (, FR-8 from guard G2). Sam Newman: the fixed status vocabulary was never checked against the contracts that already exist.
finding.wrong_outcome: (, FR-8 from guard G2). Sam Newman: the fixed status vocabulary was never checked against the contracts that already exist.

e1.text: keep their fields and add the missing ones
e1.context:
| WC-1 | **No prompt before the agent is ready.** Nothing in the launch path (wrapper, hook, startup command) may wait on a person before Claude's input box is ready. Any such prompt must fall back on its own well inside the readiness limit (default 60 s). | Launch setup, not commands | `EVIDENCE.md:39` (worker-start failed at `agent_readiness` behind a session-name prompt); `EVIDENCE.md:45,56` (passes with a 30 s fallback; above about 45 s it fails again); `CAPS:44-45` (60 s default, `--timeout-ms` per start) |
| WC-2 | **No person-blocking step in unattended mode.** Under `--unattended` the command never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends its turn on a chat question or `[yes / no]` offer, and never says STOP AND WAIT. Each gate resolves one of three ways, listed per command in section 3: (a) a documented default; (b) a value the caller supplied as a flag; (c) **blocked**: the command writes its report with `status: blocked` and the exact question, and stops. | Command | Gates per command at `INV-A:76-83`, `INV-B:292`; a worker waiting on a prompt is "healthy", so a stall is invisible (`CAPS:52`, `CAPS:129`); a plain chat offer also stalls (`INV-A:62`) |
| WC-3 | **Questions go to the coordinator, not to a local prompt.** When a gate would resolve as blocked and the worker session holds a preamble, the session may instead ask the coordinator once with the preamble's `ask` command, wait, then re-invoke or resume the command with the answer as a flag. On an `ask` timeout it resumes the same message ID and never creates a duplicate. No heartbeat is sent while blocked in `ask`. | Worker session | `CAPS:58-61` (`[H:ask]` lines 3-5, 23-24; `[G]` lines 80-82); `CAPS:64` (`[G:worker-contract]` lines 10-11) |
| WC-4 | **One report file, known before dispatch, written on every outcome.** In unattended mode the command writes `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, where `<output-dir>` is the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`). It follows the return-contract pattern several commands already use and carries at least: `status` (one of `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`, `blocked`), `command` (the exact command line), `report_path` (the main human-readable deliverable, if any), `artifacts` (every other file written), and, when blocked, `blocked_question`. It is written on success, failure, blocked and partial outcomes, including stops before any other output exists. Commands that already write a contract keep their fields and add the missing ones. The worker passes the contract path as `worker_done --report-path`. Orca does not check the file, so the coordinator opens it. | Command writes; worker reports; coordinator reads | `CAPS:72-74` (`--report-path` only with real values); `CAPS:79` (Orca's handling of the file is UNVERIFIED); existing models: `sk/sc-workflow-protocol/refs/return-contract.md:3-19,41` via `INV-B:272`, `sk/sc-brainstorm-protocol/SKILL.md:335` via `INV-A:97` |
| WC-5 | **Outcome mapping.** The worker sends `worker_done` exactly once from its own top-level session. `--outcome failed` when the report says `failed` or `blocked`, or no report exists; `--outcome succeeded` otherwise, including `partial` and including an audit whose verdict is FAIL (the audit itself succeeded). The first sentence of the body states the report's status and verdict. | Worker session | `CAPS:73` (`[G]` lines 88-90, "Never encode failure only in prose"); `CAPS:76-77` |
| WC-6 | **Resume or safe re-run.** A retry worker (`worker-start --retry-of`) must not corrupt the first attempt's output. A command either resumes from its on-disk state when given its resume flag, or, if it has none, writes each run into a fresh output directory so a re-run starts clean. Section 3 names which applies per command. | Command | `CAPS:116` (retry and circuit breaker); resume mechanisms in column (e) of `INV-A:35-55`, `INV-B:31-52` |
| WC-7 | **Run at the top level, never inside a subagent.** The worker runs the command directly in its own session; it never wraps the command in an Agent-tool subagent. Lifecycle messages (`heartbeat`, `ask`, `check`, `worker_done`) are sent only by that top-level session, never by a subagent. A command's own Agent-tool fan-out stays as it is. | Worker session | `sk/sc-pr-submit-protocol/SKILL.md:37-39` (top-level rule); `CAPS:159-161`; `INV-A:95` (nesting loses tools at Claude Code's depth limit) |

outcome_follows.instructions: Does an implementer who follows the texts in `evidence` as written build the outcome described in `finding.wrong_outcome`?

criteria.true: Read as written, the texts in `evidence` lead an implementer to the outcome in `finding.wrong_outcome`.
criteria.false: Read as written, the texts in `evidence` lead an implementer to a different outcome from the one in `finding.wrong_outcome`.

texts_conflict.instructions: Do `evidence.e1.text` and `evidence.e2.text` require incompatible outcomes for the same situation?

criteria.true: No implementation can satisfy `evidence.e1.text` and `evidence.e2.text` in the same situation.
criteria.false: One implementation can satisfy both `evidence.e1.text` and `evidence.e2.text`, for example because they apply to different conditions.

evidence_sufficient.instructions: Do the texts in `evidence` contain everything needed to judge whether the outcome in `finding.wrong_outcome` follows, without other parts of the document?

criteria.true: The quoted texts and their surrounding lines in `evidence` are enough to judge the claimed outcome.
criteria.false: Judging the claimed outcome needs a part of the document that `evidence` does not include, such as a definition or an exception stated elsewhere.

Any such prompt must fall back on its own well inside the readiness limit (default 60 s). | Launch setup, not commands | `EVIDENCE.md:39` (worker-start failed at `agent_readiness` behind a session-name prompt); `EVIDENCE.md:45,56` (passes with a 30 s fallback; above about 45 s it fails again); `CAPS:44-45` (60 s default, `--timeout-ms` per start) |
| WC-2 | **No person-blocking step in unattended mode.** Under `--unattended` the command never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends its turn on a chat question or `[yes / no]` offer, and never says STOP AND WAIT. Each gate resolves one of three ways, listed per command in section 3: (a) a documented default; (b) a value the caller supplied as a flag; (c) **blocked**: the command writes its report with `status: blocked` and the exact question, and stops. | Command | Gates per command at `INV-A:76-83`, `INV-B:292`; a worker waiting on a prompt is "healthy", so a stall is invisible (`CAPS:52`, `CAPS:129`); a plain chat offer also stalls (`INV-A:62`) |
| WC-3 | **Questions go to the coordinator, not to a local prompt.** When a gate would resolve as blocked and the worker session holds a preamble, the session may instead ask the coordinator once with the preamble's `ask` command, wait, then re-invoke or resume the command with the answer as a flag. On an `ask` timeout it resumes the same message ID and never creates a duplicate. No heartbeat is sent while blocked in `ask`. | Worker session | `CAPS:58-61` (`[H:ask]` lines 3-5, 23-24; `[G]` lines 80-82); `CAPS:64` (`[G:worker-contract]` lines 10-11) |
| WC-4 | **One report file, known before dispatch, written on every outcome.** In unattended mode the command writes `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, where `<output-dir>` is the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`). It follows the return-contract pattern several commands already use and carries at least: `status` (one of `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`, `blocked`), `command` (the exact command line), `report_path` (the main human-readable deliverable, if any), `artifacts` (every other file written), and, when blocked, `blocked_question`. It is written on success, failure, blocked and partial outcomes, including stops before any other output exists. Commands that already write a contract keep their fields and add the missing ones. The worker passes the contract path as `worker_done --report-path`. Orca does not check the file, so the coordinator opens it. | Command writes; worker reports; coordinator reads | `CAPS:72-74` (`--report-path` only with real values); `CAPS:79` (Orca's handling of the file is UNVERIFIED); existing models: `sk/sc-workflow-protocol/refs/return-contract.md:3-19,41` via `INV-B:272`, `sk/sc-brainstorm-protocol/SKILL.md:335` via `INV-A:97` |
| WC-5 | **Outcome mapping.** The worker sends `worker_done` exactly once from its own top-level session. `--outcome failed` when the report says `failed` or `blocked`, or no report exists; `--outcome succeeded` otherwise, including `partial` and including an audit whose verdict is FAIL (the audit itself succeeded). The first sentence of the body states the report's status and verdict. | Worker session | `CAPS:73` (`[G]` lines 88-90, "Never encode failure only in prose"); `CAPS:76-77` |
| WC-6 | **Resume or safe re-run.** A retry worker (`worker-start --retry-of`) must not corrupt the first attempt's output. A command either resumes from its on-disk state when given its resume flag, or, if it has none, writes each run into a fresh output directory so a re-run starts clean. Section 3 names which applies per command. | Command | `CAPS:116` (retry and circuit breaker); resume mechanisms in column (e) of `INV-A:35-55`, `INV-B:31-52` |
| WC-7 | **Run at the top level, never inside a subagent.** The worker runs the command directly in its own session; it never wraps the command in an Agent-tool subagent. Lifecycle messages (`heartbeat`, `ask`, `check`, `worker_done`) are sent only by that top-level session, never by a subagent. A command's own Agent-tool fan-out stays as it is. | Worker session | `sk/sc-pr-submit-protocol/SKILL.md:37-39` (top-level rule); `CAPS:159-161`; `INV-A:95` (nesting loses tools at Claude Code's depth limit) |

e1.text: src/superclaude/core
e1.context:
### 2.1 Terms
- **Worker run**: a session that received an Orca preamble carrying a Task ID and a Dispatch ID. Only such a session may send lifecycle messages; a session the user started, inside or outside Orca, is an ordinary session (`CAPS:148`, `[G]` lines 38 and 41).
- **Unattended mode**: the behaviour a command switches to when its caller passes `--unattended`. It is the only command-side change the contract asks for besides report files and resume. It names no Orca command, so the same mode serves any caller that has no person at the keyboard. How the mode is selected (flag versus detecting the preamble) is open decision D1 in section 9; this spec is written for the recommended flag.
- **Contract file**: one shared document, proposed as `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, installed to `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`. Core `.md` files install to `~/.claude/` (`src/superclaude/cli/install_core.py:4,33`; `CLAUDE.md:83,408`), and the new name must be added to `KNOWN_CORE_FILES` (`src/superclaude/cli/install_core.py:13-24`). Each changed command adds a short `## Unattended mode` section that lists only its own gate resolutions and report file and points to the installed contract path, so the shared rules are written once.

### 2.2 Requirements
Each requirement says what the command must do, what the worker session (the top-level agent that received the preamble) must do, and the evidence.

e1.context:
| WC-1 | **No prompt before the agent is ready.** Nothing in the launch path (wrapper, hook, startup command) may wait on a person before Claude's input box is ready. Any such prompt must fall back on its own well inside the readiness limit (default 60 s). | Launch setup, not commands | `EVIDENCE.md:39` (worker-start failed at `agent_readiness` behind a session-name prompt); `EVIDENCE.md:45,56` (passes with a 30 s fallback; above about 45 s it fails again); `CAPS:44-45` (60 s default, `--timeout-ms` per start) |
| WC-2 | **No person-blocking step in unattended mode.** Under `--unattended` the command never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends its turn on a chat question or `[yes / no]` offer, and never says STOP AND WAIT. Each gate resolves one of three ways, listed per command in section 3: (a) a documented default; (b) a value the caller supplied as a flag; (c) **blocked**: the command writes its report with `status: blocked` and the exact question, and stops. | Command | Gates per command at `INV-A:76-83`, `INV-B:292`; a worker waiting on a prompt is "healthy", so a stall is invisible (`CAPS:52`, `CAPS:129`); a plain chat offer also stalls (`INV-A:62`) |
| WC-3 | **Questions go to the coordinator, not to a local prompt.** When a gate would resolve as blocked and the worker session holds a preamble, the session may instead ask the coordinator once with the preamble's `ask` command, wait, then re-invoke or resume the command with the answer as a flag. On an `ask` timeout it resumes the same message ID and never creates a duplicate. No heartbeat is sent while blocked in `ask`. | Worker session | `CAPS:58-61` (`[H:ask]` lines 3-5, 23-24; `[G]` lines 80-82); `CAPS:64` (`[G:worker-contract]` lines 10-11) |
| WC-4 | **One report file, known before dispatch, written on every outcome.** In unattended mode the command writes `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, where `<output-dir>` is the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`). It follows the return-contract pattern several commands already use and carries at least: `status` (one of `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`, `blocked`), `command` (the exact command line), `report_path` (the main human-readable deliverable, if any), `artifacts` (every other file written), and, when blocked, `blocked_question`. It is written on success, failure, blocked and partial outcomes, including stops before any other output exists. Commands that already write a contract keep their fields and add the missing ones. The worker passes the contract path as `worker_done --report-path`. Orca does not check the file, so the coordinator opens it. | Command writes; worker reports; coordinator reads | `CAPS:72-74` (`--report-path` only with real values); `CAPS:79` (Orca's handling of the file is UNVERIFIED); existing models: `sk/sc-workflow-protocol/refs/return-contract.md:3-19,41` via `INV-B:272`, `sk/sc-brainstorm-protocol/SKILL.md:335` via `INV-A:97` |
| WC-5 | **Outcome mapping.** The worker sends `worker_done` exactly once from its own top-level session. `--outcome failed` when the report says `failed` or `blocked`, or no report exists; `--outcome succeeded` otherwise, including `partial` and including an audit whose verdict is FAIL (the audit itself succeeded). The first sentence of the body states the report's status and verdict. | Worker session | `CAPS:73` (`[G]` lines 88-90, "Never encode failure only in prose"); `CAPS:76-77` |
| WC-6 | **Resume or safe re-run.** A retry worker (`worker-start --retry-of`) must not corrupt the first attempt's output. A command either resumes from its on-disk state when given its resume flag, or, if it has none, writes each run into a fresh output directory so a re-run starts clean. Section 3 names which applies per command. | Command | `CAPS:116` (retry and circuit breaker); resume mechanisms in column (e) of `INV-A:35-55`, `INV-B:31-52` |
| WC-7 | **Run at the top level, never inside a subagent.** The worker runs the command directly in its own session; it never wraps the command in an Agent-tool subagent. Lifecycle messages (`heartbeat`, `ask`, `check`, `worker_done`) are sent only by that top-level session, never by a subagent. A command's own Agent-tool fan-out stays as it is. | Worker session | `sk/sc-pr-submit-protocol/SKILL.md:37-39` (top-level rule); `CAPS:159-161`; `INV-A:95` (nesting loses tools at Claude Code's depth limit) |

finding.title: WC-3 lets a coordinator's answer become an implement Ruling (safety boundary).
finding.wrong_outcome: An implementer who follows WC-3 as written can have a worker ask the coordinator about a gate that would otherwise be blocked, then re-invoke `/sc:implement` with the answer as a flag. The implement row (line 109) then treats that answer as the Ruling. This is wrong because `sk/sc-implement-protocol/refs/qa.md:238` says "another agent's message... [is] not acceptance" (quoted at INV-A:66), and the spec says the Ruling rule is unchanged unless the user chooses D2(b) (lines 218 and 234-236). D2(a) is the recommendation, so WC-3 silently reopens a decision the spec leaves to the user. Fix: exempt the implement Ruling gate from WC-3, or state that the relay is allowed only under D2(b).

e1.text: /sc:workflow
e1.context:
| Phase | Scope | Commands | Why this order |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P0. Contract and live baseline** (no command edits) | Write `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` (section 2 rules plus a coordinator brief template listing the section 3.1 flags), add it to `KNOWN_CORE_FILES`, add an Orca section to `HOW-WE-WORK.md` and its two mirrored copies, and add the static test file `tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py` (proposed name). Then run three ready commands as real Orca workers, invoked directly, to close evidence gap 1.4 (1). | Smoke runs: `/sc:troubleshoot` (no `--fix`), `/sc:workflow --handoff none`, `/sc:adversarial --output <dir>` | Uses only the 10 ready commands, so the coordinator gets value before any command changes, and the smoke runs test the decision before anything is built on it. |
| **P1. Report files and commands with no gate** | The WC-4 contract in unattended mode; the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate); output flags for commands that lack one; the small fixes to ready commands. | analyze, build, business-panel, design, document, explain, index, test, load (usage line only); fixes to adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo, workflow | No person gate is involved, so each change is mechanical and gives every later phase a report file to check. |
| **P2. Gate conversion** | Each default-on gate resolves per its section 3 row; WC-10 wait splitting for cli-eval. | auggie-review, cleanup, improve, cli-eval, cli-portify, recommend, research, review-translation, spec-panel, task, tasklist, reflect, release-split, tdd, troubleshoot | The main blocker class (`INV-A:96`, `INV-B:292`). These changes touch no safety rule and add no outward capability; where a command has an outward default (auggie-review posting, task's `commit`/`push` and committed TFEP report), P2 only turns it off under `--unattended` (WC-9). |
| **P3. Interface drift and shared state** | Reconcile command and skill where they disagree; make memory writes parallel-safe. | roadmap, validate-roadmap, validate-tests, save | These are defects today regardless of Orca (`INV-B:294,296`); the coordinator cannot predict their report path until they are fixed. |

e2.text: including stops before any other output exists
e2.context:
| WC-1 | **No prompt before the agent is ready.** Nothing in the launch path (wrapper, hook, startup command) may wait on a person before Claude's input box is ready. Any such prompt must fall back on its own well inside the readiness limit (default 60 s). | Launch setup, not commands | `EVIDENCE.md:39` (worker-start failed at `agent_readiness` behind a session-name prompt); `EVIDENCE.md:45,56` (passes with a 30 s fallback; above about 45 s it fails again); `CAPS:44-45` (60 s default, `--timeout-ms` per start) |
| WC-2 | **No person-blocking step in unattended mode.** Under `--unattended` the command never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends its turn on a chat question or `[yes / no]` offer, and never says STOP AND WAIT. Each gate resolves one of three ways, listed per command in section 3: (a) a documented default; (b) a value the caller supplied as a flag; (c) **blocked**: the command writes its report with `status: blocked` and the exact question, and stops. | Command | Gates per command at `INV-A:76-83`, `INV-B:292`; a worker waiting on a prompt is "healthy", so a stall is invisible (`CAPS:52`, `CAPS:129`); a plain chat offer also stalls (`INV-A:62`) |
| WC-3 | **Questions go to the coordinator, not to a local prompt.** When a gate would resolve as blocked and the worker session holds a preamble, the session may instead ask the coordinator once with the preamble's `ask` command, wait, then re-invoke or resume the command with the answer as a flag. On an `ask` timeout it resumes the same message ID and never creates a duplicate. No heartbeat is sent while blocked in `ask`. | Worker session | `CAPS:58-61` (`[H:ask]` lines 3-5, 23-24; `[G]` lines 80-82); `CAPS:64` (`[G:worker-contract]` lines 10-11) |
| WC-4 | **One report file, known before dispatch, written on every outcome.** In unattended mode the command writes `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, where `<output-dir>` is the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`). It follows the return-contract pattern several commands already use and carries at least: `status` (one of `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`, `blocked`), `command` (the exact command line), `report_path` (the main human-readable deliverable, if any), `artifacts` (every other file written), and, when blocked, `blocked_question`. It is written on success, failure, blocked and partial outcomes, including stops before any other output exists. Commands that already write a contract keep their fields and add the missing ones. The worker passes the contract path as `worker_done --report-path`. Orca does not check the file, so the coordinator opens it. | Command writes; worker reports; coordinator reads | `CAPS:72-74` (`--report-path` only with real values); `CAPS:79` (Orca's handling of the file is UNVERIFIED); existing models: `sk/sc-workflow-protocol/refs/return-contract.md:3-19,41` via `INV-B:272`, `sk/sc-brainstorm-protocol/SKILL.md:335` via `INV-A:97` |
| WC-5 | **Outcome mapping.** The worker sends `worker_done` exactly once from its own top-level session. `--outcome failed` when the report says `failed` or `blocked`, or no report exists; `--outcome succeeded` otherwise, including `partial` and including an audit whose verdict is FAIL (the audit itself succeeded). The first sentence of the body states the report's status and verdict. | Worker session | `CAPS:73` (`[G]` lines 88-90, "Never encode failure only in prose"); `CAPS:76-77` |
| WC-6 | **Resume or safe re-run.** A retry worker (`worker-start --retry-of`) must not corrupt the first attempt's output. A command either resumes from its on-disk state when given its resume flag, or, if it has none, writes each run into a fresh output directory so a re-run starts clean. Section 3 names which applies per command. | Command | `CAPS:116` (retry and circuit breaker); resume mechanisms in column (e) of `INV-A:35-55`, `INV-B:31-52` |
| WC-7 | **Run at the top level, never inside a subagent.** The worker runs the command directly in its own session; it never wraps the command in an Agent-tool subagent. Lifecycle messages (`heartbeat`, `ask`, `check`, `worker_done`) are sent only by that top-level session, never by a subagent. A command's own Agent-tool fan-out stays as it is. | Worker session | `sk/sc-pr-submit-protocol/SKILL.md:37-39` (top-level rule); `CAPS:159-161`; `INV-A:95` (nesting loses tools at Claude Code's depth limit) |

finding.title: The `/sc:spec-panel` row (section 3.2) rests on a premise the command file contradicts
finding.wrong_outcome: an implementer who follows the row adds a second `--output` flag and a second `## Unattended mode` section to a command that already has both, so the command ends with two report-path flags (`--output <file>` and `--report-dir <dir>`) and two conflicting unattended definitions, one of which WC-4 does not describe.

e1.text: --output-dir
e1.context:
| WC-1 | **No prompt before the agent is ready.** Nothing in the launch path (wrapper, hook, startup command) may wait on a person before Claude's input box is ready. Any such prompt must fall back on its own well inside the readiness limit (default 60 s). | Launch setup, not commands | `EVIDENCE.md:39` (worker-start failed at `agent_readiness` behind a session-name prompt); `EVIDENCE.md:45,56` (passes with a 30 s fallback; above about 45 s it fails again); `CAPS:44-45` (60 s default, `--timeout-ms` per start) |
| WC-2 | **No person-blocking step in unattended mode.** Under `--unattended` the command never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends its turn on a chat question or `[yes / no]` offer, and never says STOP AND WAIT. Each gate resolves one of three ways, listed per command in section 3: (a) a documented default; (b) a value the caller supplied as a flag; (c) **blocked**: the command writes its report with `status: blocked` and the exact question, and stops. | Command | Gates per command at `INV-A:76-83`, `INV-B:292`; a worker waiting on a prompt is "healthy", so a stall is invisible (`CAPS:52`, `CAPS:129`); a plain chat offer also stalls (`INV-A:62`) |
| WC-3 | **Questions go to the coordinator, not to a local prompt.** When a gate would resolve as blocked and the worker session holds a preamble, the session may instead ask the coordinator once with the preamble's `ask` command, wait, then re-invoke or resume the command with the answer as a flag. On an `ask` timeout it resumes the same message ID and never creates a duplicate. No heartbeat is sent while blocked in `ask`. | Worker session | `CAPS:58-61` (`[H:ask]` lines 3-5, 23-24; `[G]` lines 80-82); `CAPS:64` (`[G:worker-contract]` lines 10-11) |
| WC-4 | **One report file, known before dispatch, written on every outcome.** In unattended mode the command writes `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, where `<output-dir>` is the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`). It follows the return-contract pattern several commands already use and carries at least: `status` (one of `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`, `blocked`), `command` (the exact command line), `report_path` (the main human-readable deliverable, if any), `artifacts` (every other file written), and, when blocked, `blocked_question`. It is written on success, failure, blocked and partial outcomes, including stops before any other output exists. Commands that already write a contract keep their fields and add the missing ones. The worker passes the contract path as `worker_done --report-path`. Orca does not check the file, so the coordinator opens it. | Command writes; worker reports; coordinator reads | `CAPS:72-74` (`--report-path` only with real values); `CAPS:79` (Orca's handling of the file is UNVERIFIED); existing models: `sk/sc-workflow-protocol/refs/return-contract.md:3-19,41` via `INV-B:272`, `sk/sc-brainstorm-protocol/SKILL.md:335` via `INV-A:97` |
| WC-5 | **Outcome mapping.** The worker sends `worker_done` exactly once from its own top-level session. `--outcome failed` when the report says `failed` or `blocked`, or no report exists; `--outcome succeeded` otherwise, including `partial` and including an audit whose verdict is FAIL (the audit itself succeeded). The first sentence of the body states the report's status and verdict. | Worker session | `CAPS:73` (`[G]` lines 88-90, "Never encode failure only in prose"); `CAPS:76-77` |
| WC-6 | **Resume or safe re-run.** A retry worker (`worker-start --retry-of`) must not corrupt the first attempt's output. A command either resumes from its on-disk state when given its resume flag, or, if it has none, writes each run into a fresh output directory so a re-run starts clean. Section 3 names which applies per command. | Command | `CAPS:116` (retry and circuit breaker); resume mechanisms in column (e) of `INV-A:35-55`, `INV-B:31-52` |
| WC-7 | **Run at the top level, never inside a subagent.** The worker runs the command directly in its own session; it never wraps the command in an Agent-tool subagent. Lifecycle messages (`heartbeat`, `ask`, `check`, `worker_done`) are sent only by that top-level session, never by a subagent. A command's own Agent-tool fan-out stays as it is. | Worker session | `sk/sc-pr-submit-protocol/SKILL.md:37-39` (top-level rule); `CAPS:159-161`; `INV-A:95` (nesting loses tools at Claude Code's depth limit) |

e2.context:
### 2.1 Terms
- **Worker run**: a session that received an Orca preamble carrying a Task ID and a Dispatch ID. Only such a session may send lifecycle messages; a session the user started, inside or outside Orca, is an ordinary session (`CAPS:148`, `[G]` lines 38 and 41).
- **Unattended mode**: the behaviour a command switches to when its caller passes `--unattended`. It is the only command-side change the contract asks for besides report files and resume. It names no Orca command, so the same mode serves any caller that has no person at the keyboard. How the mode is selected (flag versus detecting the preamble) is open decision D1 in section 9; this spec is written for the recommended flag.
- **Contract file**: one shared document, proposed as `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, installed to `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`. Core `.md` files install to `~/.claude/` (`src/superclaude/cli/install_core.py:4,33`; `CLAUDE.md:83,408`), and the new name must be added to `KNOWN_CORE_FILES` (`src/superclaude/cli/install_core.py:13-24`). - **Worker run**: a session that received an Orca preamble carrying a Task ID and a Dispatch ID. Only such a session may send lifecycle messages; a session the user started, inside or outside Orca, is an ordinary session (`CAPS:148`, `[G]` lines 38 and 41).
- **Unattended mode**: the behaviour a command switches to when its caller passes `--unattended`. It is the only command-side change the contract asks for besides report files and resume. It names no Orca command, so the same mode serves any caller that has no person at the keyboard. How the mode is selected (flag versus detecting the preamble) is open decision D1 in section 9; this spec is written for the recommended flag.
- **Contract file**: one shared document, proposed as `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, installed to `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`. Core `.md` files install to `~/.claude/` (`src/superclaude/cli/install_core.py:4,33`; `CLAUDE.md:83,408`), and the new name must be added to `KNOWN_CORE_FILES` (`src/superclaude/cli/install_core.py:13-24`). Each changed command adds a short `## Unattended mode` section that lists only its own gate resolutions and report file and points to the installed contract path, so the shared rules are written once.

### 2.2 Requirements
Each requirement says what the command must do, what the worker session (the top-level agent that received the preamble) must do, and the evidence.
e1.text: ## Unattended mode

e2.context:
| WC-1 | **No prompt before the agent is ready.** Nothing in the launch path (wrapper, hook, startup command) may wait on a person before Claude's input box is ready. Any such prompt must fall back on its own well inside the readiness limit (default 60 s). | Launch setup, not commands | `EVIDENCE.md:39` (worker-start failed at `agent_readiness` behind a session-name prompt); `EVIDENCE.md:45,56` (passes with a 30 s fallback; above about 45 s it fails again); `CAPS:44-45` (60 s default, `--timeout-ms` per start) |
| WC-2 | **No person-blocking step in unattended mode.** Under `--unattended` the command never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends its turn on a chat question or `[yes / no]` offer, and never says STOP AND WAIT. Each gate resolves one of three ways, listed per command in section 3: (a) a documented default; (b) a value the caller supplied as a flag; (c) **blocked**: the command writes its report with `status: blocked` and the exact question, and stops. | Command | Gates per command at `INV-A:76-83`, `INV-B:292`; a worker waiting on a prompt is "healthy", so a stall is invisible (`CAPS:52`, `CAPS:129`); a plain chat offer also stalls (`INV-A:62`) |
| WC-3 | **Questions go to the coordinator, not to a local prompt.** When a gate would resolve as blocked and the worker session holds a preamble, the session may instead ask the coordinator once with the preamble's `ask` command, wait, then re-invoke or resume the command with the answer as a flag. On an `ask` timeout it resumes the same message ID and never creates a duplicate. No heartbeat is sent while blocked in `ask`. | Worker session | `CAPS:58-61` (`[H:ask]` lines 3-5, 23-24; `[G]` lines 80-82); `CAPS:64` (`[G:worker-contract]` lines 10-11) |
| WC-4 | **One report file, known before dispatch, written on every outcome.** In unattended mode the command writes `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`, where `<output-dir>` is the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`). It follows the return-contract pattern several commands already use and carries at least: `status` (one of `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`, `blocked`), `command` (the exact command line), `report_path` (the main human-readable deliverable, if any), `artifacts` (every other file written), and, when blocked, `blocked_question`. It is written on success, failure, blocked and partial outcomes, including stops before any other output exists. Commands that already write a contract keep their fields and add the missing ones. The worker passes the contract path as `worker_done --report-path`. Orca does not check the file, so the coordinator opens it. | Command writes; worker reports; coordinator reads | `CAPS:72-74` (`--report-path` only with real values); `CAPS:79` (Orca's handling of the file is UNVERIFIED); existing models: `sk/sc-workflow-protocol/refs/return-contract.md:3-19,41` via `INV-B:272`, `sk/sc-brainstorm-protocol/SKILL.md:335` via `INV-A:97` |
| WC-5 | **Outcome mapping.** The worker sends `worker_done` exactly once from its own top-level session. `--outcome failed` when the report says `failed` or `blocked`, or no report exists; `--outcome succeeded` otherwise, including `partial` and including an audit whose verdict is FAIL (the audit itself succeeded). The first sentence of the body states the report's status and verdict. | Worker session | `CAPS:73` (`[G]` lines 88-90, "Never encode failure only in prose"); `CAPS:76-77` |
| WC-6 | **Resume or safe re-run.** A retry worker (`worker-start --retry-of`) must not corrupt the first attempt's output. A command either resumes from its on-disk state when given its resume flag, or, if it has none, writes each run into a fresh output directory so a re-run starts clean. Section 3 names which applies per command. | Command | `CAPS:116` (retry and circuit breaker); resume mechanisms in column (e) of `INV-A:35-55`, `INV-B:31-52` |
| WC-7 | **Run at the top level, never inside a subagent.** The worker runs the command directly in its own session; it never wraps the command in an Agent-tool subagent. Lifecycle messages (`heartbeat`, `ask`, `check`, `worker_done`) are sent only by that top-level session, never by a subagent. A command's own Agent-tool fan-out stays as it is. | Worker session | `sk/sc-pr-submit-protocol/SKILL.md:37-39` (top-level rule); `CAPS:159-161`; `INV-A:95` (nesting loses tools at Claude Code's depth limit) |

finding.title: The `/sc:spec-panel` row (section 3.2) rests on a premise the command file contradicts
finding.wrong_outcome: an implementer who follows the row adds a second `--output` flag and a second `## Unattended mode` section to a command that already has both, so the command ends with two report-path flags (`--output <file>` and `--report-dir <dir>`) and two conflicting unattended definitions, one of which WC-4 does not describe.

outcome_follows.instructions: Does an implementer who follows the texts in `evidence` as written build the outcome described in `finding.wrong_outcome`?

criteria.true: Read as written, the texts in `evidence` lead an implementer to the outcome in `finding.wrong_outcome`.
criteria.false: Read as written, the texts in `evidence` lead an implementer to a different outcome from the one in `finding.wrong_outcome`.

texts_conflict.instructions: Do `evidence.e1.text` and `evidence.e2.text` require incompatible outcomes for the same situation?

criteria.true: No implementation can satisfy `evidence.e1.text` and `evidence.e2.text` in the same situation.
criteria.false: One implementation can satisfy both `evidence.e1.text` and `evidence.e2.text`, for example because they apply to different conditions.

evidence_sufficient.instructions: Do the texts in `evidence` contain everything needed to judge whether the outcome in `finding.wrong_outcome` follows, without other parts of the document?

criteria.true: The quoted texts and their surrounding lines in `evidence` are enough to judge the claimed outcome.
criteria.false: Judging the claimed outcome needs a part of the document that `evidence` does not include, such as a definition or an exception stated elsewhere.
